Subject: Bridge update: preliminary findings

On Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:22:37 -07:00 Michael Grant wrote:
> Tara — thanks for the alert and logs. We're standing up a focused bridge now (ops + SRE + account) and will update every 30 minutes or sooner.

Quick technical summary:
- Observed symptom: high p95/p99 token latencies and 500s from the model shard service in us-west-2 between 08:40–09:10 PDT.
- Preliminary root cause: a recent autoscaling policy change combined with an uneven sequence-length distribution caused a hotspot on a subset of GPUs, exhausting KV cache memory on affected nodes. When the cache thrash hit, requests stalled and triggered retries which exacerbated queuing.
- Evidence: error traces attached, and kv cache snapshots show rapid eviction spikes.

Immediate mitigations applied (~09:30 PDT):
1) Pinned traffic away from affected shard pool (fallback routing to stable pool).
2) Temporarily lowered batch size for the text-gen route to reduce tail latency.
3) Throttled retries at the gateway.

Status: error rate down ~70% since 09:35, but we are still monitoring for residual latency blips. We're collecting full traces and a kv cache dump for the postmortem.

I'll post a technical write-up and timeline when we have the KV dump parsed.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Aurora service stability update — executive summary and next steps

Tara — quick executive summary for your leadership: 

What happened (tl;dr):
- Between ~08:40–09:10 PDT on 2026-08-21 we recorded elevated tail latencies and 500 errors for the text-generation route serving Aurora workloads in us-west-2. This was driven by a KV cache exhaustion on a subset of GPU shards after an autoscaling policy edge case combined with atypical sequence-length distribution in traffic.

Actions we took:
- Routed traffic away from affected shards and enabled a stable model variant fallback (~09:30 PDT).
- Reduced server-side batch sizes and throttled gateway retries to prevent re-amplification.
- Restored normal error-rate and latency profile; observed error rate improvement ~70% within 20 minutes.

Customer impact:
- Short window of degraded response times and elevated error rates impacting some feature requests. No data exfiltration suspected.

Next steps:
1) Postmortem: Rishi's team will deliver a technical postmortem and timeline within 72 hours.
2) Preventative fixes: we will harden autoscaling policy guards, implement KV cache pressure alerts, and add a routing fallback that triggers earlier under similar patterns.
3) Compensation: Grace will coordinate any service credit or billing adjustments if you believe user-facing impact merits it.
4) Follow-up meeting: propose a 30-minute sync for Tuesday 2026-08-24 10:00 PDT to walk the postmortem and mitigation plan.

If you'd like a brief for your C-suite I can provide a 1-page summary. Apologies for the disruption — we'll follow through on the action items and keep you closely informed.
